title: Bootstrapping autoregressive duration models
abstract: arXiv:2607.28294v2 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: This paper develops bootstrap methods for likelihood-based inference in autoregressive conditional duration (ACD) models, where the sample size is endogenously determined by durations observed over a fixed time span. This feature fundamentally shapes the asymptotic framework, particularly so when the durations do not have finite expectation. Building on recent limit theory for heavy-tailed and integrated ACD processes, we analyze recursive bootstrap schemes that either fix the time span (yielding a random sample size) or fix the number of durations (yielding a random time span). We establish a bootstrap theory for ACD models that links naturally to renewal theory with random sample sizes. For the fixedcount bootstrap, we prove first-order validity in the finite-mean and boundary cases and characterize the random limiting bootstrap distribution in the infinite-mean case. tldr: 本文为自回归条件持续期（ACD）模型建立了递归自助法理论，分别考虑固定时间跨度（随机样本量）和固定持续期数量（随机时间跨度）两种方案，证明了固定数量自助法在有限均值情形下的一阶有效性，并刻画了无限均值情形下的随机极限自助分布。
en_tdlr: This paper develops recursive bootstrap theory for autoregressive conditional duration (ACD) models under random sample sizes or random time spans, proving first-order validity of the fixed-count bootstrap in the finite-mean case and characterizing the random limiting bootstrap distribution in the infinite-mean case.
